clue.text: Supporter of half-day closing

parts.note: half of the word Friday, its first three letters, an abbreviation for the day
a closing is an end

explanation.surface: A fan of shops shutting for the afternoon once a week.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of FRIDAY is FRI, the usual short form of the day; the clue's 'half-day closing' is the old British early-closing day.
explanation.definitionFit: A friend backs you up, so is a supporter in the broad sense.

clue.text: Breakfast ingredient fresh from fridge, for example

indicators.note: fresh suggests something newly made, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An item for the morning meal taken straight out of the fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges FRIDGE together with EG, the abbreviation for 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried egg is a classic item of a cooked breakfast.

clue.text: Prays for urchins without learning

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: mischievous children are imps
lore is traditional learning

explanation.surface: Someone begs on behalf of uneducated street children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not in the modern sense of lacking, so it signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore is to beg earnestly, which is what praying for something amounts to.

clue.text: He didn't take single boarders

parts.note: the biblical ark-builder let animals aboard only in pairs, so no single passenger boarded

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the ark's builder took the animals in two by two, never one alone.

clue.text: Second drink I have makes me frisky

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
contracted, I have is I've

explanation.surface: A drinker says a second glass of port livens them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportive means playful and lively, a synonym of frisky.

clue.text: A drilling site

parts.note: drilling read as soldiers practising marching, not boring holes for oil

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers do their drill on the parade ground, so it is the place for drilling.

clue.text: Part or parts of the fish left in

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: roe is the egg mass of a fish

explanation.surface: Asking which piece of the fish has been left on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A role is an actor's part in a play.

clue.text: Fools do, and it is silly

indicators.note: silly suggests muddled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fools behave like this, and it is silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silly' rearranges DO and IT IS; 'and' just joins the two lots of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiots are foolish people, the plural noun matching fools.

clue.text: Proceeded to take legal action in extremity

indicators.note: in places the legal word inside the word for extremity

parts.note: an extremity is an end
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Someone driven to the last resort decided to go to court.
explanation.definitionFit: Ensued means followed on or came next, as events proceed.

clue.text: Not out of touch but performing publicly?

definitions.meaning: in football a ball not over the touchline is still ...
an actor in a play is performing publicly

explanation.definitionFit: In play is the sporting term for a live ball, and taken literally it means appearing in a play.

clue.text: Girls maybe right to accept glamorous underwear

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: fillies is old slang for girls, from young female horses

explanation.surface: Women perhaps happy to receive fancy lingerie as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Frillies is a colloquial word for frilly women's underwear.

clue.text: Reckless villain can show solicitude

parts.note: a villain may be called a devil
may and can both express permission
to care is to show concern

explanation.surface: Even a careless rogue is capable of kindness.
explanation.definitionFit: Devil-may-care describes someone cheerfully careless of risk, so reckless.

clue.text: One is put out when shown this

definitions.text: One is put out when shown this

parts.words: One is put out when shown this
parts.note: to be shown it is to be told to leave, which may leave one put out, offended, as well as outside

explanation.definitionFit: Being shown the way out of a room means being made to leave by it.

clue.text: Hazards of drivers and divers

parts.note: motorists meet curves in the road, and divers who surface too fast suffer decompression sickness, both known by one word

explanation.definitionFit: The same word names curves in a road and the decompression sickness divers fear.

clue.text: Pen a note making personal complaint

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Writing a letter to make a complaint of one's own.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small infection on the eyelid, an ailment of one person.

clue.text: Forger's block

parts.note: a forger here is a smith who forges metal, not a counterfeiter, and his block is the iron one he hammers on

explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith shapes hot metal on this heavy iron block.

clue.text: Box kite?

definitions.meaning: old slang for an aeroplane, like kite, especially a rickety one

explanation.definitionFit: A crate is a packing case, and both crate and kite are slang for an aircraft.

clue.text: Inexperienced hands reveal growing talent

parts.note: green means raw or inexperienced
fingers stand in for hands

explanation.surface: Novice workers turn out to have a developing gift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing talent' looks like a rising star but means skill at growing plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Green fingers is the British idiom for a knack with plants.

clue.text: Certain to be optimistic

definitions.meaning: hopeful, looking on the bright side

explanation.definitionFit: Positive means both sure of something and hopeful in outlook.

clue.text: Calculating a pudding mixture

indicators.note: a mixture stirs things together, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Working out the quantities for a pudding mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding up figures is calculating a total.

clue.text: Company with some of the stocks sought by mountaineers

parts.note: a firm is a business company
the stocks were a frame holding an offender's feet, so one part of them is a hold for a foot

explanation.surface: A business holding shares that climbers want to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocks' suggests shares, but means the old punishment frame that held the feet.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber looks for a secure place to put a foot on a rock face.

clue.text: Forces servant to be a comic character

definitions.meaning: an officer's personal servant in the army
the caped crusader of comic books

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an officer's orderly and the famous comic-book hero.

clue.text: No part exchange for this customer

indicators.note: exchange swaps things round, so these letters change places

explanation.surface: A shopper is told there are no trade-ins on spare parts.
explanation.definitionFit: A patron is a regular customer of a shop or restaurant.

clue.text: Just open — so have a glass of ale

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: The pub has just opened, so let's have a beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left ajar is slightly open.

clue.text: Not standing for falsehoods

explanation.definitionFit: Lying means both reclining and telling untruths.

clue.text: Two identical notes she sings in opera

indicators.note: two identical asks for one piece written twice

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A soprano repeats the same note during an aria.
explanation.walkthrough: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Bohème.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimi is the singing heroine of Puccini's opera La Bohème.

clue.text: Steal a free ride

definitions.meaning: a ride given in someone's car

explanation.definitionFit: Lift means to steal and, in Britain, a ride offered in a car.

clue.text: Widely grown but it's not used

definitions.meaning: in ... condition means unused, as new

explanation.definitionFit: Mint is a common herb, and the word also describes something in unused condition.

clue.text: Such a seat may be alarming to M P

indicators.note: may be hints the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A constituency that worries the sitting member of parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' rearranges ALARMING; 'to M P' completes the picture and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A marginal seat is a constituency held by a small majority.

clue.text: Display by top-class band

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, the 1 read as the letter I
a ring is a band, as worn on a finger

explanation.surface: A performance by an excellent musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: An airing is a public showing or display, as of opinions.

clue.text: The naughty time when Einstein was around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters are turned about into another order

explanation.surface: A racy period in history when the physicist was alive.
explanation.walkthrough: The Naughty Nineties is the nickname of the 1890s.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1890s are known as the Naughty Nineties.

clue.text: Peter's involved with Meryl

indicators.note: involved suggests tangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Peter is in a relationship with the actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Meryl Streep is the American actress, so the surname completes the name.
